name: Spanish American wars of independence
short_desc: Independence movements and armies break Spanish rule across much of the Americas and establish new republics.
location: North America · South America · Mexico · Venezuela · Colombia · Ecuador · Peru · Bolivia · Chile · Argentina
date_note: Main campaigns, following the Oxford overview’s 1809–1825 frame. The crisis began earlier; resistance and recognition continued later. Fighting was not continuous everywhere, and Brazil’s separation from Portugal was a different process.
notes: Added after a catalog gap review on 24 October 2026. A major transformation of the political map of the Americas; the existing Bolívar biography covers only part of this wider process. Evidence and date rationale: The 1809–1825 main-campaign window follows Natalia Sobrevilla Perea’s Oxford research overview. The 1808 crisis in Spain preceded it, and later resistance, recognition and settlements extend beyond these bounds. This is a collective regional conflict window, not uninterrupted fighting in every place. Brazil’s separation from Portugal is a different process. Primary evidence: https://academic.oup.com/edited-volume/61800/chapter-abstract/546343865?login=false. Cached Wikipedia introduction and lead image provide separately attributed background. Remains review, not comprehensive factual approval.
